tweet_text:
okay this is insane, the design suggestion by Fable for touching/sensing the mesh surfaces is allowing Opus to do radical things I've never seen them able to do before and this likely generalizes to other models... the video below shows a two-shot full assembly of a completely unique modular building with 3 different modular kits that Opus had no pre-existing information about and don't come with any assembly tooling... this sensor system has the potential to drastically improve LLM environment design and their raw 3d modeling capability for tons of different models... this is done in @threejs but can likely be easily ported to other engines... i'll post the kits Opus used to do this below... the only reason it was two-shot, btw, is because Opus 4.8 got nervous after initially making the pipes too thin and paused before doing the fire escapes... 

this sensor system lets the models ingest arbitrary geometry and figure out how write the code to procedurally assemble it into correct looking outputs, it drastically supplements their visual checks and really helps close the gap

the most amazing part about this is that Opus figured out how to mash kit pieces into other meshes based on their visible elements with the sensors, just from me saying this "also did you use your sensors on the door and the bottom ... this is a really interesting question because this about using your sensors to understand when you should mash geometry into some other geometry to hide it when building from premade meshes, i'm not going to explain what i mean in more detail there, i want to see if you can figure it out" after the initial hesitation
